John James

Republican candidate for Governor / Lt. Governor, Michigan · Open seat

U.S. Representative for Michigan's 10th Congressional District; Army veteran and businessman

John James is a Republican U.S. Representative for Michigan's 10th Congressional District and a former Army aviation officer. President Trump endorsed him, and he won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary for governor, defeating businessman Perry Johnson and former Attorney General Mike Cox. His running mate for lieutenant governor is Jay DeBoyer, and he faces Democrat Jocelyn Benson and minor-party candidates in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where James stands

Education
Says Michigan's low reading scores and school performance are the top education problem. Wants the governor to have more control over the state's education system so schools can be held accountable.
Parental rights and school sports
Supports parental rights in schools and says girls' school sports should be protected. Campaigned with a parent who is suing a school district over classroom displays.
Taxes and school choice
Campaigned on an Education Freedom Tax Credit and on repealing the state income tax.
Economy and cost of living
Says his campaign focuses on the economy, education, infrastructure and public safety. Argues that families face high costs, including energy prices, and that Michigan needs a change in direction.
Tariffs and trade
Says he disagrees with President Trump on tariff policy and has pushed back on the administration's tariffs against Canada.
Data centers
Talked about data center development and wants communities to have a stronger voice in decisions that affect them.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Michigan's 10th Congressional District (2023–present)
  • Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan, 2018 and 2020
  • U.S. Army aviation officer, Ranger-qualified; combat veteran
  • Businessman
  • Won the 2026 Republican primary for governor (August 4, 2026)
